topic: Rev J + the guarded tracker G4 in the whole-pen physics simulation, rerun with causal sensing (study X, sim2j headline card)
citation: This study's simulation (rebaseline/sim2j_cards.py): sim2 / MuJoCo whole Rev J pen, sim2j firmware, the frozen G4 tracker, causal Hall velocity, delayed measured contact, 80 Hz inner loop
task_or_setup: Essential tremor 8-12 Hz x 1-2 mm on the H1 hand, v2 synthetic test writers 0-5 on their first test seed (the historical cases, paired), 'return library' after a 4 s rest; the same cases with the legacy optimistic flags on the same code, and with the historical firmware contact channel (exact reproduction)
comparator: The same pen with the nose held (ordinary-pen column); perfect knowledge; the historical rows
key_quantitative_findings: Ink error with G4 / held nose: causal 0.612 (writer bootstrap 0.596-0.627; 24 cases), legacy flags 0.620, historical 0.628; words of 10 7.5 -> 10.0 (historical 7.7 -> 10.0); letters 8.0 -> 9.4; perfect knowledge 0.169; clean writing moved 0.0 um (max 0.0); mean power 1.54 -> 1.52 W (legacy 2.36 W)
units_and_conditions: Ratio of rms ink error to the clean-ink letters (lower is better); words and letters read by the app's recogniser, of 10; W incl. 0.077 W electronics; SIMULATION
limitations: Synthetic writers and tremor; one seed per writer; the static ball load of the C1S nose still dominates power; the nib is Rev J's, not the balanced nib; no measurement
relevance_to_design: Whether the explainer's biggest positive result survives realistic sensing
transferability_reason: Simulation on the stated inputs; not a measurement of a pen or of any person
design_implication: G4's synthetic-tremor card is reported with causal sensing; legacy numbers become an optimistic bound (DEC-070)

topic: The balanced nib (Rev K and the 24 mm / 1.5 mm candidate) in sim2 with causal contact, DEC-066's 40/46 Hz servo and corrected loads (study X; synthetic-input half of EXP-E23)
citation: This study's simulation (rebaseline/bnib_rerun.py): study B's sim2 set-up (bnib/sim.py) with nonlinear wire force (revk/feasibility.wire_anchor) and 8.07 mN guide rolling drag per step

comparator: Study B's published B1 (80/100 Hz, linear wires, no drag, true-contact gate)
key_quantitative_findings: Rev K corrected: ink ratio G4 0.566, perfect knowledge 0.379, words 5.8 -> 9.2 of 10, nib power 20.5 mW, clean writing moved 0.0 um. 1.5 mm candidate: G4 0.521, perfect knowledge 0.273, words 6.0 -> 9.2, 32.1 mW
units_and_conditions: Ratios of rms ink error to the held nib's; words of 10 (app recogniser); mW copper loss at the x-axis force constant; SIMULATION
limitations: Synthetic inputs; isotropic force constant in sim2 (weaker axis and disk minimum as CALC scalings); guide drag coefficient and wire material unmeasured; no carrier structural modes
